writer.name: Claude Opus 5.5, the hypnosis guide lane's writer (the splices and their fixes; the words are Emulate's)

findings.label: B7 short landing at paragraph end
examples: If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop.
findings.reason: The linter sees the draft alone. In the article the short line is either not the paragraph's end (the stop lines go on after "quiet") or is the fallback's own point ("Don't fake it.", his inner child guide's "no faking required"), not a summing-up line.

findings.label: D9 follows the source order
examples: 1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order (agreement 1.00); fine if each part notices something; check T13 and T09 in the tell ledger
findings.reason: It is Emulate's rewrite of the passage it replaces, so it follows that passage's points in order by design, with Emulate's own asides and turns ("if I can put it that way", "of course", "just", "!").

findings.label: E36/E41 heavy second person
findings.reason: The guide speaks to the reader as "you" throughout; these lines give the reader one step or one check inside a paragraph that is not a run of coaching lines.

findings.label: O30 a phrase said three or more times in one paragraph (gate, 2026-10-07: my "a commitment they make as adults" "gave P22 its fourth "as adults""; Joel: "take out second adults that's obvious"): keep it only where the repeat does a job
examples: "you say" 3 times: Remind yourself that if you say 'stop' at any time, the induction will end. / If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less. / If you say '
findings.reason: "you say" names each word the reader can say, one per sentence: 'stop', 'less', 'quiet', as his published "“Stop” ends the exercise; “less” reduces the demand; “quiet” stops the words." The repeat is the instruction.
